subject: Renewal and capacity uplift — pricing options
thread_messages:
From: Mike Hollis <mike.hollis@solarwave.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@solarwave.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal & capacity uplift — initial ask

Hi Stephanie,

Hope you’re well. Our current agreement with Redwood runs through 31-Jan-2027. As we build out the new ML inference pipeline we expect baseline token consumption to roughly double across Q1–Q2 next year.

Before we start budgeting / procurement I wanted to surface the high-level asks so we can understand constraints on both sides:
- We expect ~2x baseline capacity by March 2027 (steady-state).
- Procurement needs: a 12-month price hold at or near current effective per-token rate, or a defined discount schedule tied to committed volumes.
- We’d like a one-time credit or invoice offset to help cover migration costs and the transition month where usage spikes.
- Flex for burst capacity (we’ll need short-term bursts during large model retrains).

Priya (cc) will run procurement and legal. Timeline: procurement wants a firm commercial by mid-Dec to finish approvals. Can Redwood share a few commitment/price hold options we can review? Also include any constraints on true-ups / overage rates.

I’ve attached a consumption extract for Q1–Q3 (summary). Happy to jump on a call next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Mike
Head of Infrastructure
SolarWave Inc.

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 10:03 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:

Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uplift — initial ask

Hi Mike — thanks for the details and the file, that’s very helpful.

Short answer: yes, we can design a renewal that balances a 12-month price hold with increase in committed capacity. Options I suggest we model:
1) 12-month price hold + staged commit increase. Customer commits to 1.6x baseline for 12 months; we hold the unit price for that window and provide an option to step to 2.0x at a pre-agreed uplift.
2) 12-month price hold + one-time migration credit applied as an invoice credit (applied Q1).
3) Full 2.0x commit for a deeper up-front discount but with a shorter price-hold (9 months).

I’ll assemble a short offer sheet with numbers and send to you + Priya. If Dec 10 as your internal signature deadline is required, let’s aim to have a commercial out by Nov 24 so your procurement has a week to review.

Attaching a draft SOW and an initial offer spreadsheet. Can you confirm Priya is the procurement contact and whether legal wants redlines on our standard amendment or a brand-new SOW?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa — forwarding SolarWave ask. Key points:
- They want a 12-month price hold at or near current effective rate and expect ~2x consumption by March.

- Procurement timeline: mid-Dec signature target.

My proposed approach: give them a middle ground (1.6x commit + 12mo price hold + $150k bridging credit applied as invoice credit). If they sign for full 2x, we can extend a deeper discount but shorter price hold. Need margin and approval guardrails. Also note they will want clear true-up mechanics and an overage multiplier.

Attaching consumption extract and offer sheet.

— Stephanie

On Sun, Nov 22, 2026 at 11:17 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal & capacity uplift — SolarWave (pricing guidance)

Thanks Steph — I like the middle-ground approach. My suggested commercial structure (handy for the offer sheet):

Summary offer (Option A - recommended):
- Commitment: 1.6x baseline committed tokens/year (baseline = FY26 rolling average).
- Price: 18% discount on our standard committed unit price, applied for 12 months (price-hold window).
- Bridging credit: $150,000 one-time invoice credit applied in Q1 after signature.
- Burst buffer: an optional burst pool (200k tokens/month) at a fixed overage price (set at the committed unit price * 1.25).
- True-up: annual true-up with either invoice or credit applied (mutually agreed).
- Overage beyond burst: billed monthly at 1.5x committed rate.
- Conditions: credit contingent on signature of amendment and commit schedule; credit amortized across first two invoices if needed.

Option B (Aggressive uplift):
- Commit to 2.0x baseline; 22% discount; 9-month price hold; no bridging credit (or reduced $50k credit).

Notes / internal guardrails:
- Approve Option A for AE signature (preserves margin vs Option B).
- Confirm finance ok with $150k credit being applied as one-time invoice credit; suggests carve in HubSpot notes and coordinate with billing ops.

I’ll add these rows into the Offer_Sheet and link to the HubSpot deal. Draft amendment language (price hold clause + true-up window) is in the DocuSign draft I'm preparing.

Ben
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Hi Mike / Priya — thanks again for the details and patience while we pulled internal approvals. Attached is our recommended commercial that balances your desire for predictability with a pragmatic commit profile. Summary below. Full offer sheet + draft amendment are attached.

Recommended (Option A — ready for signature):
- Commit: 1.6x baseline committed tokens/year.
- Effective unit price: current committed price less 18% (applied for 12 months).
- Bridging credit: $150,000 one-time invoice credit (applied to first Q1 invoice).
- Burst pool: optional 200k tokens/month at committed unit price * 1.25 (available on request).
- True-up: annual true-up; overage beyond burst billed at 1.5x committed rate.
- Price hold: 12 months from effective amendment date. After 12 months, pricing reverts to standard committed pricing unless re-negotiated.

If SolarWave wants to lock a deeper discount we can discuss Option B (2.0x commit, 22% discount, 9-month price hold) — we put that in the offer sheet for completeness.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached Offer_Sheet and Amendment.
2) If OK, sign the amendment via DocuSign (link below). We ask for signature by Dec 10 to align with your procurement timeline.
3) On signature we’ll schedule a kickoff for engineering and a migration runbook review.
